instructions.original_snippets: NEVER access process.argv directly when Commander.js is available
instructions.content: Never read process.argv directly for a value Commander.js already parses; declare it as an argument or option instead.

instructions.original_snippets: NEVER use .action() callback without handling errors
instructions.content: Never leave an async action handler without try/catch; unhandled rejections crash the process with no useful message.

instructions.original_snippets: NEVER add .parseAsync() without await
instructions.content: Never call parseAsync() without await; Commander v8+ needs the await or the process exits before async actions finish.

instructions.original_snippets: NEVER define commands with positional arguments and options that share ambiguous prefixes
instructions.content: Never leave positional arguments and options in an order where Commander could misparse an option value as a positional argument.

instructions.original_snippets: NEVER use program.opts() to read option values inside a subcommand
instructions.content: Never read program.opts() inside a subcommand action; each .command() has its own option scope and the parent's opts() silently returns the wrong values.

instructions.original_snippets: ALWAYS pass complete typed options objects to services (never individual properties)
instructions.content: Always pass the complete typed options object into a service function rather than individual properties.

instructions.original_snippets: Define TypeScript interfaces for all options
instructions.content: Define a TypeScript interface for every command's options object.

instructions.original_snippets: Export commands as Command instances from subcommand modules
instructions.content: Export each subcommand as a named Command instance from its own module.

instructions.original_snippets: Use .addCommand() to attach subcommands to parent Command
instructions.content: Attach subcommands to the parent program with .addCommand().

instructions.original_snippets: Use parseAsync() for async action handlers
instructions.content: Use parseAsync() instead of parse() whenever any action handler is async.

instructions.original_snippets: Validate options in action handlers
instructions.content: Validate option values inside the action handler before acting on them.

instructions.original_snippets: Provide clear descriptions for all commands/options
instructions.content: Give every command and option a clear description string.

instructions.original_snippets: Use TypeScript for type safety
instructions.content: Write the CLI in TypeScript for type safety.

instructions.original_snippets: Handle errors gracefully with try/catch
instructions.content: Wrap action handler logic in try/catch.

instructions.original_snippets: Use kebab-case for option names
instructions.content: Use kebab-case for multi-word option flags, not camelCase.

instructions.original_snippets: Provide sensible defaults for optional options
instructions.content: Give optional options sensible defaults rather than making everything required.

instructions.original_snippets: Create barrel exports for commands (commands/index.ts)
instructions.content: Re-export all command modules from a commands/index.ts barrel file.

instructions.original_snippets: Test CLI with different argument combinations
instructions.content: Exercise the CLI with a range of valid and invalid argument combinations in tests.

instructions.original_snippets: Use .exitOverride() for testing
instructions.content: Call program.exitOverride() in tests so Commander throws instead of calling process.exit().

instructions.original_snippets: NEVER pass individual option properties to services (pass complete typed object)
instructions.content: Never destructure the options object and forward individual properties to a service function.

instructions.original_snippets: DON'T pass options piecemeal (e.g., service(opts.a, opts.b, opts.c))
instructions.content: Do not call a service with a long list of individual option arguments.

instructions.original_snippets: Don't use parse() with async handlers (use parseAsync())
instructions.content: Do not use parse() when any action handler is async; use parseAsync().

instructions.original_snippets: Don't ignore error handling in action handlers
instructions.content: Do not leave action handler errors unhandled.

instructions.original_snippets: Don't use camelCase in CLI flags (use kebab-case)
instructions.content: Do not define CLI flags in camelCase.

instructions.original_snippets: Don't forget to specify option argument types (<required> vs [optional])
instructions.content: Do not omit angle-bracket/square-bracket argument-type markers when declaring arguments.

instructions.original_snippets: Don't mix positional arguments with options ambiguously
instructions.content: Do not order positional arguments and options so that parsing becomes ambiguous.

instructions.original_snippets: Don't forget to call program.parse() or program.parseAsync()
instructions.content: Do not omit the call to program.parse() or program.parseAsync(); without it, no arguments are ever processed.

instructions.original_snippets: Don't use global state in action handlers
instructions.content: Do not rely on module-level mutable state inside action handlers.

instructions.original_snippets: Don't suppress built-in help text without good reason
instructions.content: Do not disable Commander's built-in help output without a specific reason.

instructions.original_snippets: Don't forget to version your CLI
instructions.content: Do not ship a CLI without a --version flag.

instructions.original_snippets: Don't make all options required (use sensible defaults)
instructions.content: Do not mark every option as required; prefer sensible defaults.
